Alex Mealer

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 9, Harris County, Texas · Open seat

Small business owner (welding supply company); former oil and gas finance executive; U.S. Army veteran

Alex Mealer is the Republican nominee for Texas' 9th Congressional District, a seat redrawn in 2025 that covers east Harris County and Liberty County. She is a West Point graduate, a former Army explosive ordnance disposal officer, and the Republican nominee for Harris County judge in 2022. She led a nine-candidate Republican primary on March 3, 2026, then defeated state Rep. Briscoe Cain in the May 26 runoff.

Where Mealer stands

Border security and immigration
Says she wants to strengthen border security, including by opposing spending bills that would cut funding for Border Patrol and immigration enforcement.
Drug cartels and law enforcement
Supports combating drug cartels and backing law enforcement. Argues the open border has enabled cartels and human trafficking.
Port Houston and Ship Channel infrastructure
Proposes protecting and expanding the Houston Ship Channel and Port Houston. Calls infrastructure such as port dredging a core function of government that the port needs to stay commercially competitive.
Taxes and regulation
Pledges to cut taxes and regulations, saying burdensome regulations and rising taxes hurt families and businesses in the district.
Flooding
Supports more flood mitigation projects in the district.
Elections
Says she will work to 'secure our elections' as part of her campaign platform.

Background

  • B.S., U.S. Military Academy at West Point (2007)
  • U.S. Army explosive ordnance disposal officer; combat veteran (former captain)
  • J.D. and MBA, Harvard University (2016)
  • Finance executive in the oil and gas industry
  • Co-owner of a welding supply company with her husband, Clay
  • Republican nominee for Harris County judge (2022)
  • Board member and Public Safety Chair, Metropolitan Transit Authority of Harris County (METRO) (2024–2025)
  • Republican nominee for U.S. House, Texas District 9 (2026); won the May 26, 2026 runoff over Briscoe Cain
